More precisely, if we say that the result of a sum is 8, we do not know if it results from summing 5 and 3 or 2 and 6. Following Bennett [4], we can program the sum of x and y in Janus as follows:  (x, y, x + y) if z = 0, Rsum(x, y, z) = undefined otherwise. The function Rsum : N3 → N3 is reversible because it is defined to preserve the input values. Using the very rich language of expressions of Janus, RSum simply can be from z = 0 do z+ = (x + y) loop skip until 1. As a curiosity the same function exists in a restriction of the syntax of expression that only contains successor, predecessor and an equality test.
